records.title: Shannon counting lower bound
records.statement: Almost all Boolean functions require exponentially large circuits.
hypotheses: Functions are counted nonuniformly by truth tables.
No explicit NP language is selected.
records.conclusion: Existential nonuniform circuit lower bounds hold for generic functions.
records.source_locator: Counting argument comparing truth tables with circuit descriptions
residual_hypotheses: An explicit language in NP with a superpolynomial lower bound is missing.
records.claim_boundary: Generic-function hardness does not identify SAT or any explicit NP language.

records.title: Monotone circuit lower bounds
records.statement: Explicit monotone functions have superpolynomial or exponential lower bounds against monotone circuits.
hypotheses: Circuits are monotone and exclude negation.
The function and monotone model match the theorem.
records.conclusion: Strong lower bounds hold in the monotone model.
residual_hypotheses: No lifting theorem removes the monotonicity restriction.
records.claim_boundary: Negation may provide exponential power; monotone lower bounds are not general circuit lower bounds.

records.title: AC0 lower bounds
records.statement: Parity and related explicit functions require exponential size in fixed-depth unbounded-fan-in AND/OR/NOT circuits.
hypotheses: Depth is fixed.
Gate basis is AC0.
The target function matches the theorem.
records.conclusion: Strong lower bounds hold against AC0.
records.source_locator: Switching lemma and depth-sensitive size lower bounds
residual_hypotheses: No theorem lifts AC0 lower bounds to unrestricted polynomial-size circuits or polynomial time.
records.claim_boundary: AC0 is a strict restricted circuit class.

records.title: AC0[p] lower bounds
records.statement: Incompatible modular functions require exponential size in fixed-depth circuits with MOD_p gates.
hypotheses: Depth and modulus are fixed.
The target modular function is incompatible with the gate modulus.
records.conclusion: Strong lower bounds hold against the specified AC0[p] model.
residual_hypotheses: No lifting theorem reaches general circuits.
records.claim_boundary: AC0[p] lower bounds do not settle P versus NP.

records.title: Classical terminal lower-bound or algorithm target
records.statement: Either give a uniform deterministic polynomial-time decider for an NP-complete language, or prove that an explicit language in NP has no such decider.
hypotheses: WP00 machine and encoding lock.
All hidden resource costs charged.
Full unrestricted quantifiers preserved.
records.conclusion: P=NP in the algorithm case or P!=NP in the lower-bound case.
records.quantifier_scope: all input lengths and all encoded instances
residual_hypotheses: No terminal algorithm or lower bound is known.
records.claim_boundary: This is the unresolved endpoint, not an imported theorem.

records.title: NEXP not in nonuniform ACC
records.statement: NEXP is not contained in polynomial-size nonuniform ACC circuits.
hypotheses: The target class is NEXP.
The circuit model is ACC with fixed depth and modulus regime.
Nonuniformity is retained.
records.conclusion: A major restricted-circuit lower bound holds for a class above NP.
residual_hypotheses: The class must be lowered from NEXP to NP.
The circuit model must be expanded from ACC to general circuits or uniform algorithms.
records.claim_boundary: NEXP versus ACC is not NP versus P.

records.title: Circuit-analysis algorithms imply lower bounds
records.statement: For suitable circuit classes satisfying closure and constructibility conditions, nontrivial SAT or circuit-analysis algorithms imply superpolynomial lower bounds for specified higher complexity classes.
hypotheses: The circuit class satisfies the theorem's closure properties.
The algorithm beats exhaustive search by the required amount.
Uniformity and advice conditions match.
records.conclusion: A lower bound against that circuit class follows for the theorem's target class.
records.model: circuit-specific SAT/counting algorithms and nonuniform circuits
records.quantifier_scope: the theorem's circuit class and target complexity class
residual_hypotheses: A qualifying algorithm is needed for a circuit class broad enough to matter.
The resulting target class may remain above NP.
records.claim_boundary: The transfer theorem does not make every SAT speedup a P-versus-NP separation.

records.title: Easy-witness lower bounds for NQP and restricted models
records.statement: Easy-witness lemmas sharpen algorithm-to-lower-bound transfers and yield restricted-circuit lower bounds for nondeterministic quasi-polynomial time.
hypotheses: Witness-circuit assumptions and target circuit class match the theorem.
Quasi-polynomial time and size parameters are retained.
records.conclusion: Restricted lower bounds hold for NQP or related classes.
residual_hypotheses: Descent to NP and expansion to general circuits remain open.
records.claim_boundary: NQP lower bounds do not imply NP circuit lower bounds without a new theorem.
